messages:
Jordan: quick heads-up — i'm putting together a multi-quarter plan to tighten the thin-adapter surface and amortize accumulated tech debt. high-level: 3 phases (stabilize, narrow surface, migrate) + recurring debt-amnesty windows for low-risk cleanups. want feedback before i draft an rfc.

Anika: +1. can we spell out the deprecation windows and what counts as 'low-risk'? we need objective gates (latency, error rate, deploy flakiness). :+1:

Li: would like to see rollback safety described. also need a canary strategy for any interface deletions — ideally automated.

Sam: how does this affect Dedicated customers and pinned model routes? if we change adapter args we should avoid breaking pinned contracts. we might need a compatibility shim for a quarter or two.

Maya: suggestion: each "lane" (runtime, control-plane, telemetry) elects an owner for the effort. owners run a 2-week triage to catalogue breaking surfaces, client usages, and tests coverage.

Jordan: agreed on owners. proposed owners: Anika (control-plane), Li (runtime), Sam (client compat). proposal doc: https://go/redwood/ownership-amnesty (internal). schedule: phase 1 (q3) stabilize + audit, phase 2 (q4) narrow surface + deprecations, phase 3 (q1 next yr) migrations + remove shims.

Anika: for the gates, propose numeric thresholds: latency P95 delta <= 5ms, error-rate delta <= 0.05%, no increase in tail retries. If any gate fails, pause and create a rollback patch.

Li: sample canary job we can reuse (pseudo):
```
# canary-run.sh
for region in us-west1 eu-central; do
  run_canary --service runtime-adapter --version canary-$CI_COMMIT_SHA --requests 10000 --seq-len 512
  collect_metrics --save canary-$region.json
done
analyze_canary --baseline baseline.json --canary canary-*.json
```
If analysis flags >3 regressions we auto-revert the canary route.

Sam: agree on shim window. recommend a compatibility flag that defaults to legacy for 8 weeks post rollout, then opt-in removal after usage hits 0.1% of traffic.

enginfra-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/4532: "ownership-lattice: audit plan + canary infra" (assigned: Li).

Maya: ops concern — telemetry volume could spike during migration if clients retry. add circuit-breaker and quota bump plan to runbook. also suggest a short freeze on non-critical deploys during the main cutover days.

Jordan: noted. will add circuit-breaker and deploy freeze windows in the rfc. one more thing: debt-amnesty windows — propose 2-week sprints every quarter where teams can opt into tech-debt PR fast-tracking (reduced review SLA, dedicated ci budget). thoughts?

Anika: love the amnesty idea. helps cross-team coordination. we should publish a public checklist for what qualifies (no behavior change, only cleanup, test coverage >90%).

Li: operational checklist: canary pass, smoke deploy, telemetry sanity, rollback script. we should include a one-click revert in the runbook.

Sam: comms plan: product/CS will need a short notice to Dedicated customers for any APIs we plan to deprecate. i'll own the outreach and draft notices.

Jordan: action items i captured: Jordan -> draft RFC by EOW; Anika -> metrics/gates doc; Li -> formalize canary job and GH issue follow-ups; Sam -> customer comms template; Maya -> runbook entries for circuit-breaker + deploy freeze. i'll post the first RFC draft to #architecture and link here. Thanks all. :rocket:
